notes: Schematic, axis-aligned geometry in metres (x = east, y = south). The real downtown grid is rotated roughly 45 degrees; it is drawn north-up here.
College Ave is modeled one-way westbound and Beaver Ave one-way eastbound (see https://ecode360.com/32902839).
Intermediate streets (Burrowes, Fraser, Garner, ...) are intentionally omitted; block lengths are approximate.
Allen St and Pugh St end at College Ave (campus side is not a vehicle road in this model).
Signal timings, lane assignments and turn permissions are simulation assumptions, not municipal timing plans.

selectionRule: Candidate must be a valid policy.
Screen: mean training score must beat the champion's training score.
Development score must improve on the champion by at least 1%.
Must win (lower score) on at least 50% of paired development scenarios.
Mean completion fraction may not drop by more than 0.5 percentage points.
Side-street (Allen/Pugh origin) P95 wait may not exceed champion × 1.1 + 2 s.
Overall P95 wait may not exceed champion × 1.1 + 2 s.
If several candidates pass in one round, the lowest development score becomes champion.
scoreDefinition: Primary score = total stopped vehicle-seconds (speed < 0.5 m/s inside the network, plus all time spent in external entry queues) ÷ total scheduled vehicles. Lower is better. Every controller gets the same 900 s demand horizon and 300 s drain; unfinished vehicles keep accumulating stopped time and are reported as residual backlog.

candidates.name: coord-arterial-windows-v1
candidates.hypothesis: Aligning phase-0 (arterial) green windows with platoon travel times along College WB (C_PUG->C_ALL->C_ATH) and Beaver EB (B_ATH->B_ALL->B_PUG) will reduce stops and downstream-blocking at the C_ATH/B_ATH bottlenecks and their upstream feeds, without adding net side-street delay.
candidates.explanation: Keeps all six intersections adaptive with the champion's queue-responsive parameters (minHold 16, maxGreen [50,35], weights, hysteresis 6). Enables coordination with a shared 90 s cycle and adds six gentle phase-0 windows (bonus 5, length 30 s) whose offsets encode the measured free-flow progression: College WB offsets 0/14/50 s at C_PUG/C_ALL/C_ATH (14.3 s + 35.7 s links) and Beaver EB offsets 0/36/50 s at B_ATH/B_ALL/B_PUG (35.7 s + 14.3 s links). The small bonus nudges the adaptive controller to serve arterial through movements when the downstream link is likely to be draining, reducing spillback/blocked-by-downstream time at C_ALL/C_PUG while keeping queue-responsive priority for side streets and entry queues.

candidates.name: coord-wave-100-mixedGreen
candidates.hypothesis: The champion runs all six intersections independently (no coordination), so arterial platoons on College WB and Beaver EB arrive at C_ATH/B_ATH during red and spill back. Locking a shared 100 s cycle with travel-time-derived offsets (College WB: PUG 0 -> ALL 14 -> ATH 50; Beaver EB: ATH 60 -> ALL 96 -> PUG 10) and arterial-phase coordination windows should cut stops on the two dominant bottleneck approaches and reduce spillback, which is worst in the bursty scenarios.
candidates.explanation: Structural change: coordination enabled (was off). Shared cycle 100 s (was 90). Offsets chosen from link travel times so phase-0 greens form a westbound College Ave wave (0/14/50) and an eastbound Beaver Ave wave (60/96/10); the same offsets also give overlapping Atherton NB/SB and Allen/Pugh two-way green bands because all cross links are ~10-16 s. Added six phase-0 coordination windows (length 45-50 s, bonus 10-12) to hold the arterial phase during the wave at each intersection. Raised phase-0 maxGreen to 55 s at the two Atherton bottlenecks (C_ATH, B_ATH) and kept 50 s elsewhere to clear peak platoons; minHold, hysteresis, downstream weight and queue weight unchanged (queue weighting left to the Queue Optimizer); only approaching weight nudged 0.8 -> 1.0 to value arriving platoons. Expected effects: fewer stopped veh-s at C_ATH College WB (19.8 s mean wait) and B_ATH Beaver EB (25.5 s mean wait), less spillback onto col_all_ath/bea_ath_all, better bursty-scenario scores; side-street P95 should stay near the 100-110 s champion level since cross-street windows overlap their greens and max-red service still guarantees service.

candidates.name: qr-refine-downstream-guard
candidates.hypothesis: The champion under-protects the two short receiving links (col_pug_all and bea_all_pug, 34 veh each) where spillback/blocked-by-downstream seconds are concentrated, and mildly under-weights the dominant queues at the two highest stopped-time intersections (C_ATH, B_ATH). Raising downstream weight to 1.0 at C_PUG/B_ALL/C_ALL and queue weight plus minHold at C_ATH/B_ATH should cut spillback and mainline queue delay without worsening P95 waits, with a slightly higher oldestWait to keep side streets in check.
candidates.explanation: Changes vs champion: (1) downstream weight 0.8 -> 1.0 at C_PUG, B_ALL and C_ALL, whose phase-0 receiving links are the short/storage-limited ones showing spillback and blocked-by-downstream delay; this suppresses green for a movement whose receiving link is nearly full, letting the link drain instead of spilling back into the intersection. (2) queue weight 1.0 -> 1.15 and minHold 16 -> 18 at C_ATH and B_ATH (largest stopped-veh-sec contributors, 8594 and 9694) to clear the heavy mainline queues with fewer clearance losses. (3) oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.06 at all intersections to protect side-street and overall P95 wait while queue weight rises. maxGreen, phaseBias, hysteresis (6) and coordination (disabled, 90 s) unchanged; all other intersections keep champion weights apart from oldestWait.

candidates.name: wait-downstream-gated
candidates.hypothesis: Replacing the queue-dominant score with a downstream-gated, wait-aware score (downstream 1.0, oldestWait 0.35) will stop the controller from discharging vehicles into nearly-full short receiving links (col_pug_all, bea_all_pug, ath_c_b/ath_b_c), cutting spillback and the bursty-scenario P95 that dominates the score, while the oldestWait term prevents starvation of side streets.
candidates.explanation: Changed all six adaptive intersections: downstream weight 0.8 -> 1.0 (full gating when receiving link is saturated, protects 34-veh links), queue weight 1.0 -> 0.7 and approaching 0.8 -> 0.5 (less push into blocked links), oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.35 (wait-driven fairness, targets bursty P95 and side-street P95), minHold 16 -> 12 and hysteresis 6 -> 4 (faster reaction to burst arrivals), maxGreen [50,35] -> [45,30] (shorter maximum green so a saturated phase cannot hold through while its downstream is blocked). Coordination left disabled as in champion.

candidates.name: refine-waitweight-hyst
candidates.hypothesis: The champion under-weights the longest current wait (0.04) and uses a fairly high hysteresis (6), so side streets (Allen/Pugh NB, Beaver EB at B_ATH) and bursty tails accumulate long waits before service. Raising oldestWait weight and trimming hysteresis should cut P95/tail waits and side-street starvation without hurting throughput.
candidates.explanation: Changed on all six intersections: weights.oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.10; hysteresis 6 -> 4. Kept minHold 16, maxGreen [50,35], queue 1, approaching 0.8, downstream 0.8, phaseBias [0,0], coordination disabled. Expected: earlier preemption of long-waiting minor approaches (Allen/Pugh NB, Beaver EB at B_ATH), lower P95 and max waits in bursty scenarios, small extra switching cost offset by reduced 90 s forced-service disruptions.

candidates.name: coord-wave-wait-side-priority
candidates.hypothesis: Coordinated phase-0 green windows along College WB and Beaver EB reduce arterial stops and spillback, while stronger oldestWait weights and slight side-street phase bias at Allen/Pugh intersections prevent side-street starvation and cut P95 tails.
candidates.explanation: Enabled 90s coordination with phase-0 windows at offsets matching arterial travel times: C_PUG 0, C_ALL 14, C_ATH 50; B_ATH 0, B_ALL 36, B_PUG 50; length 30s, bonus 10. Raised oldestWait to 0.3 at C_ALL/C_PUG/B_ALL/B_PUG (0.15 at C_ATH/B_ATH) and reduced approaching to 0.7; downstream 0.9 to damp spillback. Capped minor-intersection maxGreen to [45,30] and added phaseBias +1 for side-street phase. minHold 15, hysteresis 6.

candidates.name: r2-corridor-refine-shorthold-light
candidates.hypothesis: The four undersaturated intersections (C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL, B_PUG) hold min green 16 s, which over-serves the low-volume Allen/Pugh side phases (mean waits 15-21 s, clearly starved) and delays the dominant arterial phase's return; dropping minHold to 12 s there lets the controller preempt the side phase ~4 s sooner back to the heavily queued arterial while still clearing the small side queues, cutting stopped time and P95 on those approaches. The two saturated, burst-sensitive Atherton intersections (C_ATH, B_ATH) keep minHold 16 to protect throughput and burst tails.
candidates.explanation: Changed only adaptive.minHold from 16 to 12 at C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL, B_PUG. C_ATH and B_ATH unchanged (minHold 16, maxGreen [50,35], same weights/bias/hysteresis) because they carry ~64% of stopped time and dominate the bursty tails. No change to weights, maxGreen, phaseBias, hysteresis, fixed blocks, or coordination (stays disabled). Expected: shorter cycles at light intersections, fewer seconds the arterial waits behind a nearly-empty side phase, lower side-street mean/P95 wait (Allen/Pugh NB/SB), and modest total stopped-time reduction without touching the bottlenecks where extra switching would hurt.

candidates.name: coord-atherton-aligned-90
candidates.hypothesis: Both previous coordination attempts aligned only the College WB and Beaver EB waves and ignored Atherton St, which is the second-largest source of stopped time (~13.5k veh-s/episode across C_ATH/B_ATH) on two signals only 10.4 s apart. Picking the Beaver-EB wave phase so that C_ATH and B_ATH offsets differ by exactly the Atherton travel time (10 s) makes the two crossings a two-way Atherton progression in the opposite half of the cycle, on top of the 14.3 s/35.7 s Avenue waves, cutting stops at the four dominant bottleneck approaches without adding side-street delay.
candidates.explanation: Pure coordination change on top of the champion adaptive parameters (minHold 16, maxGreen [50,35], weights, bias, hysteresis 6 all unchanged). Coordination enabled with shared cycle 90 s and a single phase-0 (arterial) green window per intersection: C_PUG offset 0 / len 45, C_ALL 14 / 42, C_ATH 48 / 48 (College WB: 0 -> 14.3 s -> 50 s release-to-arrival chain), B_ATH 38 / 48, B_ALL 74 / 42, B_PUG 88 / 45 (Beaver EB: 38 -> 74 -> 88). Bonus 15 per window (moderate so bursty demand can still preempt) and window lengths kept below the likely green so windows steer rather than dictate timing. Key new element: C_ATH(48) - B_ATH(38) = 10 s, so the derived phase-1 windows at the two Atherton crossings line up with the 10.4 s Atherton link in both directions (NB B_ATH->C_ATH and SB C_ATH->B_ATH) while the Avenue waves stay intact; fixed blocks carry the same offsets so both blocks agree.

candidates.name: qr-refine-burst-headroom
candidates.hypothesis: The two arterial entry bottlenecks (C_ATH College WB = 8594 and B_ATH Beaver EB = 9694 stopped veh-s/episode, together ~half of all stopped time) are capped at 50 s of green, forcing premature switches while their queues are still long; that premature switch-off spills back into the upstream short links (73 s of blocked-by-downstream at C_ALL). Giving those two phases burst headroom, and strengthening downstream protection on the two 34-vehicle receivers (col_pug_all at C_PUG, bea_all_pug at B_ALL), should cut stopped seconds and the bursty tail.
candidates.explanation: Changed vs champion: (1) C_ATH and B_ATH adaptive.maxGreen [50,35] -> [58,40] so the demand-responsive score can hold the heavy arterial phase (and the heavily loaded Atherton cross phase) longer during bursts instead of being forced off while queues remain; (2) C_ATH and B_ATH weights.queue 1.0 -> 1.1 and weights.oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.06 to keep the longer greens pointed at the actually-largest queue and to prevent Atherton starvation when the cap rises; (3) C_PUG and B_ALL weights.downstream 0.8 -> 0.95 to stop discharging into the two short (34-veh) receiving links that show the highest blocked-by-downstream seconds, reducing spillback at C_ALL. All other intersections, minHold 16, hysteresis 6, phaseBias, fixed blocks and the disabled coordination block stay exactly as the champion. Expected effect: lower stopped veh-s at C_ATH/B_ATH and less upstream blocking, with unchanged P95 and side-street waits (the 90 s forced-service rule still bounds maximum red).

candidates.name: r2-queue-explore-long-commit
candidates.hypothesis: Bursty scenarios dominate the score (78/46) because the champion switches phases frequently (minHold 16, hysteresis 6, maxGreen 50/35), paying 5 s clearance + 2 s startup on every switch and forcing long bursts to be served across several cycles. Committing to fewer, longer greens will clear bursts in one cycle, cutting lost time and stopped vehicle-seconds, while downstream 0.9 on the short receiving links prevents discharging into full downstream links.
candidates.explanation: Same structure as champion (all six intersections adaptive, no coordination windows). Changed: minHold 16->22 (commit longer before switching), maxGreen [50,35]->[58,42] (allow dominant arterial phase to fully clear a burst), hysteresis 6->9 (resist marginal switches away from the current green), weights queue 1.0 (same), approaching 0.8->0.75 (slightly less pre-emptive switching), oldestWait 0.04->0.05 (mild anti-starvation), downstream 0.8->0.9 (stronger receiving-link protection). Hypothesis tested: reducing switching frequency and clearance losses helps more than tight queue balancing, especially in bursty demand.

candidates.name: atherton-phase1-rebalance-v1
candidates.hypothesis: At C_ATH and B_ATH the Atherton cross-street (phase 1) carries more demand than the arterial (implied volumes ~509 vs 434 veh at C_ATH and ~579 vs 380 veh at B_ATH) yet the uniform maxGreen caps it at 35 s vs 50 s for the arterial, producing the largest sustained Atherton stopped times (B_ATH Ath NB 4965 s, C_ATH Ath SB 4095 s); rebalancing maxGreen toward phase 1 and adding a small phase-1 bias there should cut total stopped vehicle-seconds and P95 tails.
candidates.explanation: Only the two heavy Atherton intersections are changed: C_ATH maxGreen [50,35]->[48,45] and phaseBias [0,0]->[0,1]; B_ATH maxGreen [50,35]->[44,50] and phaseBias [0,0]->[0,2]. All other four intersections, all weights (queue 1, approaching 0.8, oldestWait 0.04, downstream 0.8), hysteresis 6, minHold 16 and coordination (disabled) are unchanged. Expected effect: phase 1 (Atherton NB/SB, the higher-volume cross movement at these two nodes) wins green sooner and holds it longer, draining its large queues; the low-volume Allen/Pugh side streets are untouched so their P95 should not degrade.

candidates.name: burst-relief-maxGreen-caps-v1
candidates.hypothesis: The champion caps mainline green at 50 s at the two Atherton intersections (C_ATH, B_ATH) and side-street green at 35 s everywhere; during bursts the mainline cap forces premature clearance+startup losses and spillback chains (col_all_ath/bea_in_w spillback 113 s at B_ATH, 73 s blocked-by-downstream on col_pug_all), while the 35 s side cap truncates Allen/Pugh service. Raising the mainline cap toward the simulator's own 60 s limit at the two bottlenecks, and the cross-street cap to 40 s at all intersections, is inert under light balanced flow but relieves bursts and side-street tails when dema
candidates.explanation: Changed adaptive caps only, all other levers left at champion values: C_ATH and B_ATH maxGreen [50,35] -> [60,40] (critical mainline College WB / Beaver EB can hold green until its own queue clears; side Atherton phase also gets more headroom so it is not starved by the longer mainline window); C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL, B_PUG maxGreen [50,35] -> [50,40] (Allen/Pugh NB and SB, all short 14-veh entry links, get a longer service window when they have demand, reducing side-street P95); hysteresis 6 -> 5 at all six (slightly faster reaction to a burst switching to the loaded phase); oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.06 (mild tail protection only, well below the wait-dominant values that failed in R1); queue 1.0, approaching 0.8, downstream 0.8, minHold 16 and phaseBias 0 unchanged. Coordination stays disabled (offline coordinated variants failed the dev rule). Expected: lower stopped veh-sec on the two dominant approaches and their upstream feeds in bursty scenarios, no change in light/balanced scenarios, no side-street starvation.

candidates.name: r3-corridor-refine-sidebias
candidates.hypothesis: At the four undersaturated intersections (C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL, B_PUG) the side-street phases (Allen/Pugh NB/SB) show mean waits of 15-21 s versus only 4-9 s on the arterial, i.e. they are systematically starved by the queue-dominant score; a small positive phase-1 bias lets the controller serve these small side queues sooner, cutting side-street stopped vehicle-seconds and P95 tails at negligible arterial cost (the arterial there is either lightly loaded or already downstream-limited).
candidates.explanation: Copy of champion (all six intersections adaptive, minHold 16, maxGreen [50,35], weights queue 1 / approaching 0.8 / oldestWait 0.04 / downstream 0.8, hysteresis 6, coordination off). Sole change: phaseBias [0,0] -> [0,2] at C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL, B_PUG, giving the Allen/Pugh side phases a +2 score bonus so they preempt the arterial slightly earlier. C_ATH and B_ATH (the two saturated bottlenecks) are left untouched to protect arterial throughput and burst tails. Expected effect: side-street stopped time (~7.3k veh-s/episode across those four intersections) drops with minimal arterial penalty, lowering total stopped veh-s/veh and side-street P95.

candidates.name: hybrid-fixed4-arterial-band
candidates.hypothesis: Keeping all six signals adaptive means the four low-volume signals (C_PUG, C_ALL, B_ALL, B_PUG) restart their phases at unpredictable times, so platoons on the 132 m College WB (C_PUG->C_ALL) and Beaver EB (B_ALL->B_PUG) links arrive mid-red and the short 34-veh receivers spill back. Putting those four on one shared 90 s cycle with offsets equal to the 14.3 s link travel gives the platoons a deterministic green band, while C_ATH and B_ATH keep adaptive control to absorb bursts.
candidates.explanation: Mode change (new structural hypothesis): C_PUG, C_ALL, B_ALL, B_PUG switch from adaptive to fixed-time, all on the same 90 s cycle so their offsets are meaningful. Offsets are set to the measured link travel time of the downstream movement: C_PUG 0 -> C_ALL 14 (14.3 s) -> C_ATH 52 implied, and B_ALL 36 -> B_PUG 50 (14.3 s). Splits are arterial-heavy where the cross street is light (C_PUG 0.70/0.30, C_ALL 0.65/0.35) and near-balanced where the cross street carries real demand (B_ALL 0.50/0.50, B_PUG 0.55/0.45, keeping Beaver EB slightly favored so the 34-veh bea_all_pug receiver does not block B_ALL discharge). The two bottleneck intersections C_ATH and B_ATH stay adaptive with the champion's exact adaptive parameters (minHold 16, maxGreen 50/35, queue 1, approaching 0.8, oldestWait 0.04, downstream 0.8, hysteresis 6) so burst tails are still handled responsively; their unused fixed blocks are set to consistent 90/0.6/0.4 values. Coordination stays disabled (windows are added to adaptive scores and three previous window-based attempts did not generalize to dev). Expected effect: fewer mid-red arrivals and less spillback on col_pug_all and bea_all_pug, lower stopped time at the four

candidates.name: r3-queue-refine-atherton-arterial-boost
candidates.hypothesis: The two Atherton intersections dominate stopped time (C_ATH College WB 8594, B_ATH Beaver EB 9694 veh-s/episode) and their arterial queues spill back into the long receiving links col_all_ath/bea_ath_all, which in turn blocks the upstream arterials (C_ALL College WB blockedByDownstream 73 s). Giving phase 0 a little more green headroom and a small score bias at exactly these two bottlenecks should drain those links, cutting both the bottleneck stopped time and the upstream blocking, without touching the undersaturated Allen/Pugh intersections that carry the dev-sensitive side-street demand.
candidates.explanation: Only C_ATH and B_ATH change; all other intersections and coordination stay identical to the champion. C_ATH.adaptive.maxGreen: [50,35] -> [55,35]; C_ATH.adaptive.phaseBias: [0,0] -> [1.5,0]. B_ATH.adaptive.maxGreen: [50,35] -> [55,35]; B_ATH.adaptive.phaseBias: [0,0] -> [1.5,0]. Rationale: the arterial phase at the two entry bottlenecks is the single largest source of stopped vehicle-seconds and its spillback propagates upstream; a modest green-headroom increase plus a small bias lets it clear bursts in fewer cycles and drains col_all_ath/bea_ath_all, reducing C_ALL blockedByDownstream. Side-street (Atherton) maxGreen is left at 35 so it is not starved, and the four undersaturated intersections are untouched to avoid the dev regression seen when minHold was shortened there.
decision: passed the rule, but r3-queue-explore scored better on development

candidates.name: atherton-arterial-share-bias
candidates.hypothesis: Adaptive phase scores sum over ALL approaches in a phase, so the two-approach Atherton phases at C_ATH and B_ATH get a structural scoring advantage over the single-approach arterial phases, starving the two dominant entry bottlenecks (C_ATH College WB = 8594 stopped veh-s/ep, B_ATH Beaver EB = 9694, plus 113 s spillback). Adding a small arterial phaseBias at exactly those two intersections restores green share to match true demand, and raising the arterial maxGreen to 60 lets bursts finish in one green instead of across cycles; the four undersaturated intersections stay untouched so side-stree
candidates.explanation: Changed only the two saturated Atherton intersections: C_ATH maxGreen [50,35] -> [60,35], phaseBias [0,0] -> [2,0]; B_ATH maxGreen [50,35] -> [60,40], phaseBias [0,0] -> [3,0]. minHold 16, hysteresis 6, weights (queue 1, approaching 0.8, oldestWait 0.04, downstream 0.8) unchanged everywhere. Expected effects: (1) longer, more frequent arterial greens at the two tightest entry bottlenecks cut their queue and the upstream blocked-by-downstream/spillback chains (col_all_ath, bea_in_w); (2) bias alone is small relative to the 90 s forced-service cap and to phase 1 maxGreen 35/40, so Atherton SB/NB red stays bounded (~65-70 s max) and side-street P95 should not blow up; (3) untouched minor intersections preserve their current low arterial waits (5.8-9 s).

candidates.name: r3-robustness-refine-sidewait-undersat
candidates.hypothesis: The champion's uniform oldestWait weight (0.04) means the low-volume side streets at the four undersaturated Allen/Pugh crossings (Allen NB 18-21 s mean wait, Pugh NB 17.2 s) are skipped in favour of the arterial whenever the arterial has any queue, so they only get served near the 90 s force-serve threshold and drive both the side-street P95 (104 s) and part of the tail. Raising oldestWait only at those four intersections (which have spare capacity and short cycles, so extra switches cost almost no lost time) should get long-waiting side-street vehicles served within a normal cycle, cutting s
candidates.explanation: Single-lever, targeted refinement of the champion. Changed: adaptive.weights.oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.10 at C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL and B_PUG only (the four undersaturated crossings where Allen/Pugh NB-SB show the largest side-street mean waits: B_ALL Allen NB 21 s / 2212 stopped veh-s, C_ALL Allen NB 18 s, C_PUG Pugh NB 17.2 s, B_PUG Pugh NB 17.2 s). At a 60 s side-street wait the wait term now contributes ~6 score points, i.e. about the hysteresis margin, so a starved side street preempts around 60 s of red instead of waiting for the 90 s force-serve. C_ATH and B_ATH keep oldestWait 0.04, minHold 16, maxGreen [50,35], hysteresis 6, downstream 0.8 and phaseBias [0,0], so the dominant College WB (8594 veh-s) and Beaver EB (9694 veh-s) phases are untouched and no new arterial spillback is created. No coordination change (coordination.enabled false, as in the champion); side streets at these four nodes have spare capacity so the extra switches add negligible clearance loss. Expected effect: lower side-street P95 and fewer 60-90 s side-street waits, small net reduction in total stopped vehicle-seconds, no completion loss.

candidates.name: side-demand-maxGreen-split-v1
candidates.hypothesis: The champion applies the identical maxGreen [50,35] to every intersection, but at the two Beaver cross-streets (B_ALL, B_PUG) the Allen/Pugh side phase carries MORE stopped vehicle-time than the Beaver EB arterial (B_ALL: 3065 vs 2685 veh-s; B_PUG: 2101 vs 1543 veh-s) with mean side waits of 17-21 s while the arterial runs nearly free (4.0-6.5 s).
